title: Gather Victim Host Information: Client Configurations
shortTitle: Gather Victim Host Information: Client Configurations
summary: This sub-technique covers collection of client side configuration detail rather than installed applications: operating system family and build, processor architecture, virtualisation platform, system language, locale and time zone. These values are cheap for an adversary to harvest because browsers volunteer most of them, either through request headers to a compromised or attacker controlled page or through small scripts that fingerprint the rendering behaviour of a visited site. The reason the data matters is that it steers exploit selection, since payloads must match architecture and operating system, and it also informs social engineering because language, locale and working hours shape a believable message. Compared with its parent, the emphasis moves from what software is installed to how the endpoint is configured, which is why the artefacts sit in web proxy logs, content delivery logs and unusual user agent strings rather than in service banners. Legitimate analytics and support tools collect the same fields at scale, so defenders differentiate by destination reputation, volume and whether the endpoint had any business reason to load that content.

beginner.definition: This is when an attacker collects the settings of your computers and browsers. That includes the operating system, whether it is 32 or 64 bit, the language, the time zone and whether it runs in a virtual machine. Nothing is broken or changed.
beginner.whyItMatters: These settings tell an attacker which malicious file will actually run on your machine. They also help an attacker write messages that look normal for your language and working hours. Support tools and analytics collect the same facts, so the activity hides easily among everyday traffic.
howItWorks: The attacker prepares a web page, advert or email that quietly gathers details from every visitor.
Your browser shares facts such as the operating system, browser name and language as it loads the page.
Small scripts on the page measure the screen, fonts and time zone to fill in the gaps.
The attacker records which versions and settings are common across your staff.
They choose an exploit and payload that matches those settings, so it is more likely to work.
They may also time messages to match your local working day for a more convincing approach.
beginner.example: Think of a shoe shop that keeps a note of every customer's shoe size at the door. The shop never touches the customer, but it now knows exactly which box to bring out. Client configuration collection is that note, and the exploit the attacker later chooses is the box.
takeaways: Browser and system settings leak easily when staff visit unknown or compromised sites.
Architecture, language and time zone guide both exploits and convincing fake messages.
Watch proxy logs for endpoints loading content they have no business reason to load.

objectives: List the client configuration fields that attackers commonly collect.
Explain how those fields guide exploit selection and social engineering.
Describe how a compromised or hostile web page collects configuration data.
Locate the evidence in web proxy, content delivery and endpoint browsing logs.
Separate ordinary analytics traffic from suspicious configuration collection.
